meta.audience: The reader; the fallen addressed directly from verse 17
principles: A record hidden before the fight
A roll call of the dead by ten thousands

world_behind.title: The battle is arranged by letter
world_behind.text: Verses 2 and 3 have Mormon write to the Lamanite king and receive the ground he asked for.

world_behind.title: The place is described
world_behind.text: Verse 4 says the land of Cumorah had many waters, rivers, and fountains. Mosiah 8:8 has an earlier search party cross a land of many waters covered with bones and ruins, and Ether 9:3 has Omer pass the place where the Nephites were destroyed. Three passages circle the same ground from three centuries.

world_behind.title: The records are hidden first
world_behind.text: Verse 6 has him bury everything in the hill before the armies meet. 4 Nephi 1:48 had Ammaron hide the collection at three hundred and twenty years and Mormon 2:17 had Mormon retrieve it; this is the second burial of the same records in eighty years.

world_behind.title: He keeps back a few plates
world_behind.text: Verse 6 says he gave those to his son Moroni.

world_behind.title: He is wounded and passed over
world_behind.text: Verse 10 says they went by without ending his life. Mormon 8:3 has Moroni report that his father was killed afterward, so the survival here bought only the time it took to finish the record.

world_behind.title: The dead are counted in units
world_behind.text: Verses 11 through 15 name twenty-three commanders with ten thousand each. Mormon 2:9 had Mormon meeting an army of forty-four thousand with forty-two thousand; the round ten thousands here are a unit of account rather than a headcount, and they are the largest numbers in the book.

world_behind.title: Three groups survive
world_behind.text: Verse 15 names the twenty-four survivors, a few who escaped into the south countries, and a few who deserted to the Lamanites. Mormon 8:2 reports the southern group hunted until they were all destroyed, and Moroni 9:24 had already predicted the deserters. Two of the three groups are accounted for elsewhere.

words.text: The hill and the land around it. The record uses the name nine times, eight of them in this chapter and one at Mormon 8:2. It appears nowhere in the King James Bible.
Springs, sources of water. Treated at 1 Nephi 11:25. The record uses the word once, here, and the King James Bible fifteen times. Verse 4 uses it in the description of the land.
Overwhelming fear. It appears eight times in the record, and the King James Bible twenty-nine. Verse 8 says every soul was filled with it.
A cutting tool, here a weapon. The record uses the word four times and the King James Bible not at all in this spelling. Verse 9 lists it among sword, bow, and arrow.
To decay, to crumble away. This form turns up once, here, with none in the King James Bible. Verse 21 uses the related form of bodies in corruption.
Severe mental pain. Treated at Alma 38:8. The record uses the word eleven times and the King James Bible seventeen.
Not subject to decay. Its count is twice, here and at 2 Nephi 9:13, in this book, while the King James Bible four times. Verse 21 sets it against bodies moldering in corruption.

phrases.term: I, Mormon, wrote an epistle unto the king of the Lamanites
phrases.text: The last battle begins with correspondence. Verse 3 says the request was granted.

phrases.term: In a land of many waters, rivers, and fountains
phrases.text: The only description of the place. Verse 4 adds that they hoped for an advantage there.

phrases.term: Knowing it to be the last struggle of my people
phrases.text: He states what he expected before it happened. Everything in verse 6 follows from that knowledge.

phrases.term: Save it were these few plates which I gave unto my son Moroni
phrases.text: The exception that produces the rest of the book. One handoff between father and son.

phrases.term: With that awful fear of death which fills the breasts of all the wicked
phrases.text: The waiting described from the inside. Verse 8 adds terror at the numbers.

phrases.term: I fell wounded in the midst; and they passed by me
phrases.text: Survival by being overlooked. The verse gives no reason beyond the fact.

phrases.term: The ten thousand of my people who were hewn down, being led in the front by me
phrases.text: He counts his own command first. The list that follows is twenty-three more.

phrases.term: Their flesh, and bones, and blood lay upon the face of the earth
phrases.text: The field described without figure. Verse 15 ends with the return to mother earth.

phrases.term: O ye fair ones, how could ye have departed from the ways of the Lord
phrases.text: The lament begins. The address is to people who cannot hear it.

phrases.term: Ye are gone, and my sorrows cannot bring your return
phrases.text: The limit of grief, stated plainly. Nothing in the lament changes the outcome.

phrases.term: The Eternal Father of heaven, knoweth your state
phrases.text: The last sentence of the chapter. Judgment is handed over rather than pronounced.

verses.label: v. 2–3
verses.title: A battlefield chosen by correspondence with the enemy
verses.text: The record reports the final campaign beginning with a letter: "I, Mormon, wrote an epistle unto the king of the Lamanites, and desired of him that he would grant unto us that we might gather together our people unto the land of Cumorah." Verse 3 records the request granted in one line. The site of the last battle is negotiated, not seized, and the record supplies no terms, no messenger, and no reply text, only the request and the assent.

verses.label: v. 5–6
verses.title: The provenance of the book stated inside the narrative
verses.text: The record breaks the account of the muster to explain where the volume in the reader's hands came from: "therefore I made this record out of the plates of Nephi, and hid up in the hill Cumorah all the records which had been entrusted to me by the hand of the Lord, save it were these few plates which I gave unto my son Moroni." Three collections are distinguished in one sentence, the source, the buried archive, and the excerpt handed on. The date is fixed at verse 5, "three hundred and eighty and four years," so the record dates its own compilation to the year of the battle it is describing.

verses.label: v. 10–14
verses.title: A casualty roll counted in units of ten thousand
verses.text: The record lists commanders one at a time, each with the same figure attached: Mormon's own ten thousand at verse 10, Moroni's at verse 12, Gidgiddonah's at verse 13, and then Lamah, Gilgal, Limhah, Jeneum, Cumenihah, Moronihah, Antionum, Shiblom, Shem, and Josh at verse 14. Thirteen named commands, and verse 15 adds "ten more who did fall by the sword, with their ten thousand each." Twenty-three units of ten thousand comes to two hundred and thirty thousand. The record never states that total; it supplies the addends and leaves the sum to the reader.

verses.label: v. 15
verses.title: Three exceptions itemized against the total
verses.text: Having counted the dead, the record counts who is not among them: "those twenty and four who were with me, and also a few who had escaped into the south countries, and a few who had deserted over unto the Lamanites." Two of the three groups are left unnumbered. The desertion is recorded without comment or condemnation, in the same sentence as the survivors, which is the only mention of it in the chapter.

verses.label: v. 17–19
verses.title: One adjective carrying a lament
verses.text: The record has the mourning turn on a single word, used four times in three verses: "O ye fair ones" twice in verse 17, then "O ye fair sons and daughters" and "ye fair ones" in verse 19. Between them, verse 18 states the condition that was not met, "if ye had not done this, ye would not have fallen." The lament is built out of address rather than description, with seven vocatives in verse 19 alone, and it names no cause beyond the one clause at verse 18.

chapter.title: The end is negotiated in writing
chapter.text: Verse 2 has him request the battlefield. The last stand is scheduled by mutual agreement.

chapter.title: The book is saved before the people are lost
chapter.text: Verse 6 comes before verse 7. The record is secured while there is still an army standing.

chapter.title: One exception carries everything forward
chapter.text: Verse 6 gives a few plates to Moroni. The rest of the Book of Mormon exists because of that clause.

chapter.title: He describes fear without excusing it
chapter.text: Verse 7 gives the dread to the wicked, and he is standing among them.

chapter.title: The dead are counted, not estimated
chapter.text: Verses 11 through 15 name commanders and repeat the same number. The scale is delivered by repetition.

chapter.title: He addresses people who cannot answer
chapter.text: Verses 17 through 20 are spoken to the dead. The chapter records a lament rather than a report.

chapter.title: The lament admits its own uselessness
chapter.text: Verse 20 says his sorrows cannot bring their return. He says it and keeps grieving.

chapter.title: He does not pronounce their sentence
chapter.text: Verse 22 hands them to the Father's justice and mercy. The man who watched them die refuses to say where they end.

applications.title: Ask the other side for the terms you need
applications.text: Mormon wrote to the king of the Lamanites asking for time to gather his people at Cumorah, and the request was granted. Even at the end, a plain ask made to an opponent can be answered.

applications.title: Secure what must survive before the crisis
applications.text: He buried the records while the army was still forming up. Deciding early is the whole of it.

applications.title: Keep back the small thing you can hand on
applications.text: A few plates went to his son. Small deliberate handoffs outlast large collapses.

applications.title: Count the loss by name
applications.text: He listed commanders one after another. Naming is how grief stays honest about its size.

applications.title: Say what was refused, not only what was lost
applications.text: The lament is that they rejected a Jesus who stood with open arms to receive them. Grief gets clearer when it can name what was on offer.

applications.title: Grieve without claiming to fix it
applications.text: He says his sorrows cannot bring their return and grieves anyway. Sorrow does not have to be useful.

applications.title: Add a horizon to the mourning
applications.text: After five verses of lament Mormon writes that the day soon cometh when mortality puts on immortality. He does not stop mourning; he sets it against something longer, which is a different act from cheering himself up.

applications.title: Leave the verdict where it belongs
applications.text: The closing sentence hands their state to the Father, who knows it and deals with them according to his justice and mercy. Mormon has more standing than anyone alive to pronounce on these people, and he declines to.

questions.text: What would I bury in a hill if I knew the end was coming?
What fear have I been waiting in?
When was I passed over, and what did I do with it?
What in my life is quietly returning to the earth?
Whom would I address if they could not hear me?
What loss am I trying to sorrow my way out of?
Whose state am I judging that belongs to the Father?
